title: When the Playlist Breaks
premise: Bram Crane, the quiet statistician of her high school's championship-bound soccer team, discovers coded directions hidden in her late grandmother's recipe box — instructions that reveal the team's star players have been taking performance-boosting substances funneled through the booster club. As Bram digs deeper, she realizes her best friend Marisol is implicated and that her grandmother knew decades ago when the same scheme ran under a different coach. Torn between loyalty to the team that finally made her belong and the truth her grandmother died trying to expose, Bram must publish what she knows before the state final — knowing it will shatter her friendships and possibly her own future. In the end, she tells the truth at the cost of everything except herself, and finds that real belonging survives honesty.
about_author: Gideon Vasquez is a former sports data analyst who spent six years tracking small-college athletics before turning to fiction full-time. He writes from a converted garage in Tucson, where his own grandmother's recipe box still sits on the shelf above his desk.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. We meet Bram in her element: invisible, indispensable, running probability models for Coach Danner while the team celebrates an undefeated season around her. She likes the safety of numbers. Emotional beat: contentment built on deliberate self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Sorting her grandmother Edna's belongings, Bram finds index cards among the recipes with columns of names, dates, and dosages — written like a stat sheet. The last card is dated three weeks before Edna's death. Emotional beat: unease, the first crack in grief.

chapters.title: Cross-Checking
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. She quietly matches the card names against old yearbooks and booster club records: every name connects to the soccer program across four decades. Her hands shake doing math she wishes were wrong. Emotional beat: dread disguised as diligence.

chapters.title: Marisol Knows Something
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Team captain Marisol notices Bram asking odd questions and covers for teammate Dex, who's been secretive about 'vitamin shots' from Booster dad Rick Calloway. Emotional beat: protective loyalty beginning to curdle into complicity.

chapters.title: The Booster Room
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram sneaks into the booster club office during a fundraiser and photographs ledgers showing payments routed through a 'wellness consultancy.' She's nearly caught by Coach Danner, who watches her too long. Emotional beat: adrenaline and the thrill of being seen — dangerously.

chapters.title: What Grandma Knew
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A letter tucked inside Edna's hymnal reveals she reported the same scheme in 1989 and was silenced, her family run out of town. Edna kept evidence for thirty years, waiting for someone brave enough. Emotional beat: inheritance of courage, terrifying weight.

chapters.title: Undefeated
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The team clinches a playoff berth; the town throws a rally. Marisol feels invincible — until Dex collapses at practice and everyone calls it 'cramps.' Emotional beat: euphoria undercut by denial.

chapters.title: Locker Shut
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram tests her theory against Dex's performance data: impossible statistical spikes, then decline. She drafts an anonymous email to the district and deletes it twice. Emotional beat: the cost-benefit analysis of conscience.

chapters.title: Calloway's Offer
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Rick Calloway corners Bram, praising her 'head for numbers,' and offers her a paid analytics internship — contingent on discretion. He mentions her grandmother by name. Emotional beat: flattery curdling into threat.

chapters.title: The Friend Card
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol confronts Bram about snooping; Bram shows her one recipe card. Marisol refuses to believe it, then privately checks Dex's locker and finds the vials. Emotional beat: belief arriving too late to feel like relief.

chapters.title: Split Loyalty
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Marisol begs Bram to wait until after the state final; Bram argues every game played on dope steals the title's meaning. Their ten-year friendship fractures over timing versus truth. Emotional beat: love and duty pulling opposite directions.

chapters.title: Edna's Tape
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram finds a microcassette in the box: Edna's recorded testimony naming the original coach — Danner's father — and describing how witnesses were discredited. Bram understands silence is the family inheritance she can refuse. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Someone tips off the school paper; a half-story runs, and the team closes ranks, blaming 'a traitor inside.' Marisol suspects Bram and says nothing, hating herself for it. Emotional beat: suspicion as betrayal's first symptom.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Danner and Calloway summon Bram, presenting her doctored grade records as leverage and implying college recommendations will vanish. They offer her a clean exit if she returns 'any borrowed materials.' Emotional beat: fear, and clarity about what they fear losing.

chapters.title: Dex Comes Clean
chapters.summary: Dex's POV. Hospitalized after a second collapse, Dex admits he took the injections to keep his scholarship and gives Bram the supply chain details. He asks her not to let him be the villain of the story. Emotional beat: shame transformed into testimony.

chapters.title: The Deadline
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Two days before the state final, the district announces an 'internal review' scheduled conveniently after the season. Bram realizes the system will bury itself unless she forces the issue now. Emotional beat: ticking-clock desperation.

chapters.title: What Friendship Costs
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol must choose: back Bram publicly and lose the championship she's bled for, or stay silent and lose herself. She remembers Edna from childhood — the woman who taught her free throws and never lied to her. Emotional beat: the pivot from loyalty-as-silence to loyalty-as-truth.

chapters.title: State Final
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram walks into the packed stadium before kickoff and hands the full file — cards, ledgers, tape transcript — to the referee association liaison and a local reporter as the anthem plays. The game proceeds under protest. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into stillness.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The story breaks mid-game; the final is forfeited, Danner suspended, Calloway investigated. Teammates turn on Bram in the parking lot, and Marisol steps between them — not to defend the lie, but to defend her friend. Emotional beat: grief and solidarity entangled.

chapters.title: Hearing
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. At the district hearing, Bram presents Edna's tape alongside Dex's testimony. Calloway's lawyer attacks her credibility; she answers only with numbers, calm and exact. Emotional beat: the quiet girl finally using her voice as precision instrument.

chapters.title: Aftermath Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Weeks later: sanctions handed down, scholarships protected by new oversight, Dex recovering. Bram re-reads Edna's recipe cards and adds her own final card to the box — the outcome, dated, signed. Emotional beat: mourning braided with peace.

chapters.title: New Playlist
chapters.summary: Dual POV close. Bram and Marisol drive to scatter Edna's ashes at the old 1989 field, arguing playfully about road-trip music — the friendship scarred but intact. Bram keeps her head up now, grades up, locker open. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt on truth instead of silence.
